label_systems.label: EU / UK (EN 3)
label_systems.note: Extinguisher body is red; a coloured band or zone (max 5% of surface) shows the agent: blue = ABC/dry powder, cream = foam, black = CO2, red = water, yellow = wet chemical. Fire classes are A, B, C, D, F.

label_systems.label: USA (NFPA 10)
label_systems.note: Pictograms and letter classes A, B, C, D, K are shown on the label. Colour of the cylinder is not a reliable code; read the label.

label_systems.label: Canada (ULC)
label_systems.note: Uses ABC / BC / D class ratings with numeric ratings (e.g. 2-A:10-B:C). Read the label, not the colour.

label_systems.label: India (IS 15683 / IS 2190)
label_systems.note: Red body with agent identified by label and band colour; selection and placement follow IS 2190 and the National Building Code Part 4.

fire_types.name: Ordinary Combustibles
fire_types.materials: Wood, paper, cardboard, cloth, plastics, rubber
fire_types.examples: Pallet stacks, packaging waste, office files, wooden benches
fire_types.how: Burns with flame and glowing embers; cooling with water or ABC powder works well.
fire_types.danger: Smoulders and re-ignites; hidden embers inside stacks. Watch the area for at least 30 minutes.

fire_types.name: Flammable Liquids
fire_types.materials: Petrol, diesel, solvents, paints, thinners, oils, alcohols
fire_types.examples: Spilled diesel, solvent tank, paint store, oil drip tray
fire_types.how: Vapour burns above the liquid; smother with foam, CO2 or ABC powder.
fire_types.danger: Never use a water jet: it spreads burning liquid. Vapour can flash back along the floor.

fire_types.name: Flammable Gases
fire_types.examples: Leaking LPG cylinder, acetylene hose fire, gas line rupture
fire_types.how: Stop the fuel first: close the valve or isolate supply. Only then extinguish residual flame.
fire_types.danger: Extinguishing a gas flame without stopping the leak can cause an explosion. Cylinders can BLEVE; evacuate.

fire_types.name: Electrical Equipment
fire_types.materials: Energised panels, motors, cables, transformers, switchgear
fire_types.examples: Panel board fire, overheated motor, burning cable tray
fire_types.how: De-energise if safe, then use CO2 or ABC powder. Never use water or foam on live equipment.
fire_types.danger: Electric shock risk and re-ignition. Once power is isolated it becomes a Class A fire in the burning material.

fire_types.name: Combustible Metals
fire_types.materials: Magnesium, aluminium swarf or powder, titanium, sodium, lithium metal
fire_types.examples: Magnesium chips from machining, aluminium dust fire
fire_types.how: Special dry powder (Class D) or dry sand smothers the fire.
fire_types.danger: Water, CO2 and foam can cause violent reactions or explosions. Burns at extreme temperature.

fire_types.name: Cooking Oils and Fats
fire_types.materials: Vegetable oil, animal fat, deep-fryer oil
fire_types.examples: Canteen fryer fire, kitchen hood grease fire
fire_types.how: Wet chemical extinguisher forms a soapy layer; switch off heat and cover with a fire blanket.
fire_types.danger: Water causes a violent fireball. Oil stays above auto-ignition temperature and can reignite.

extinguishers.name: ABC Dry Powder
extinguishers.notes: Versatile. Reduces visibility and leaves residue that can damage electronics. Do not use in confined spaces or on gas fires unless the leak is stopped.

extinguishers.name: Water
extinguishers.notes: Class A only. Never on electrical, oil, fat or metal fires. Water mist variants may be rated for limited electrical use; check the label.

extinguishers.name: Foam (AFFF / FFFP)
extinguishers.notes: Good for solids and liquid spills. Not for live electrical equipment because foam conducts. Not for cooking oil unless rated.

extinguishers.name: Carbon Dioxide (CO2)
extinguishers.notes: Clean agent for electrical and small liquid fires. Limited effect on solids; use short bursts. Asphyxiation risk in small rooms; discharge horn gets extremely cold, do not hold it.

extinguishers.name: Wet Chemical
extinguishers.notes: Designed for Class F / K cooking oil fires. Apply gently from a distance with the supplied lance.

extinguishers.name: Dry Powder (Class D / L2 / M28)
extinguishers.label_colour: Blue band, labelled for metal fires
extinguishers.notes: Only extinguisher for combustible metals. Apply gently to avoid scattering burning metal. Dry sand is an acceptable alternative.

pass.detail: Pull the safety pin or break the tamper seal.
Aim the nozzle at the BASE of the fire, not the flames.
Squeeze the handle to discharge the agent.
Sweep side to side across the base until the fire is out. Stay 2 to 3 metres away and keep your exit behind you.

race.detail: Rescue anyone in immediate danger only if it is safe to do so; otherwise alert responders.
Activate the nearest manual call point and call the emergency number. State location and fire type.
Close doors and windows to starve the fire of oxygen. Do not lock doors.
Fight only a small, incipient fire with the correct extinguisher; otherwise evacuate to the assembly point.

before_fighting: The alarm is raised and the fire brigade is being called.
The fire is small (about waste-bin size) and not spreading.
You have a clear exit behind you and are standing between the fire and the exit.
The extinguisher type matches the fire type and is the correct size for you to handle.
You are trained to use the extinguisher and are physically able.
Smoke is light and you can see clearly; the room is not filling with smoke.
No explosive, toxic or pressurised hazard (gas cylinders, chemicals) is involved.
do_not_fight: The fire is bigger than a waste bin or is spreading to other materials.
Smoke is thick, dark or filling the room, or heat is hard to bear.
Gas cylinders, chemicals, explosives or fuel tanks are involved or threatened.
Your exit could be blocked, or you do not have a clear escape route.
You do not know what is burning or which extinguisher to use.
The extinguisher is empty, damaged or does not discharge properly.
You feel unsafe, unwell or untrained. Evacuate and let the fire brigade handle it.

inspection.monthly_note: Carry out a visual check monthly (more often in harsh environments) and record on the tag or register. Annual servicing must be done by a competent person.

monthly.text: Extinguisher is in its designated place and visible.
monthly.fail: Moved, hidden or blocked: return it, clear access and report.

monthly.text: Access is clear, with nothing stacked within 1 metre.
monthly.fail: Obstructed: clear the path before the shift continues.

monthly.text: Safety pin is in place and the tamper seal is intact.
monthly.fail: Pin missing or seal broken: tag out and replace or recharge.

monthly.text: Pressure gauge needle is in the green zone (where fitted).
monthly.fail: Needle in red: tag out and send for service.

monthly.text: Body, hose and nozzle show no dents, rust, cracks or blockage.
monthly.fail: Damage found: remove from service and replace.

monthly.text: Label is legible and the class rating is readable.
monthly.fail: Faded or missing label: replace the extinguisher or relabel through the supplier.
Overdue: arrange servicing and provide a replacement meanwhile.

placement: Mount on wall brackets with the carrying handle 1.0 to 1.2 metres above floor (heavier units lower).
Place along escape routes and near exits, not deep inside hazard areas.
Travel distance to the nearest extinguisher should not exceed 15 to 30 metres depending on the hazard and local code.
Put the right type for the hazard: CO2 near electrical rooms, wet chemical in kitchens, Class D in metal-machining areas.
Use clear signage visible from every direction of approach.
annual: Servicing by a qualified provider with a dated tag and record.
Hydrostatic or pressure testing at the interval set by the manufacturer and local code.
Replace or recharge any unit that has been used, even partially.
Review extinguisher types and locations after any layout, process or hazard change.

rules: No hot work without a signed hot work permit.
Remove or protect combustibles within 11 metres (35 ft) or follow the permit's radius, and cover what cannot be moved with fire blankets.
A trained fire watch with the right extinguisher stays on the job; they have no other duties.
Check floors, wall openings and the level below for sparks falling or travelling.
Never weld or cut containers that held flammable material until they are cleaned and tested.
Stop work immediately if conditions change or the permit expires.
before: Inspect the area and confirm the permit is valid for this task and location.
Move combustibles; sweep floors; cover openings and cracks.
Isolate or protect nearby flammable liquids, gases and dust.
Place an extinguisher and, where needed, a hose within reach.
Brief the welder and fire watch on the alarm, exit and emergency contacts.
Test for flammable atmosphere where gas or vapour could be present.
during: Fire watch observes continuously, including sparks and slag in adjacent areas.
Keep the extinguisher unlocked and ready.
Stop work if a smell of smoke, gas or heat is noticed.
Keep the area clear of unauthorised people.
after: Fire watch remains for at least 30 minutes after work ends (or the period set by local code, up to 60 minutes).
Check adjacent rooms, behind walls and the floor below for smouldering.
Inspect again after a further 3 to 4 hours where the permit requires.
Close the permit and record the result.
Return and inspect the extinguisher; report any discharge.

drill.frequency: At least every 6 months, and once per shift cycle for night operations; additionally after any layout change, new building or significant staff change.
before: Plan the scenario, date, exit routes and the assembly point, and inform the fire brigade or security.
Assign wardens, marshals and an observer with a stopwatch.
Brief management; do not pre-announce the exact time to workers.
Check alarms, emergency lighting and exits are working and unblocked.
during: Sound the alarm and start the timer.
Wardens sweep their zones and guide people to exits; disabled staff are assisted.
Everyone goes to the assembly point; do not use lifts.
Do a headcount against the roll call and visitors list.
The observer notes delays, blocked exits, confusion and unsafe behaviour.
after: Give the all-clear and brief the workforce immediately.
Hold a debrief within 24 hours and list findings with owners and due dates.
Fix problems and update the emergency plan.
Retrain wardens where needed and file the drill record.
